steps.text: Bring the water, sugar, cinnamon, and clove to a boil in a large saucepan over high heat. Stir until the sugar has dissolved, then remove from the heat, stir in the coffee grounds, cover, and steep for 5 minutes. Stir in the vanilla and chocolate syrup, then strain through several layers of cheesecloth to remove the coffee grounds and spices. Serve with a dollop of whipped cream.

raw_recipe.headline: Rated G Mexican Coffee
raw_recipe.description: This alcohol-free, cinnamon and clove-spiced coffee has been a favorite in our house for many years.
raw_recipe.name: Rated G Mexican Coffee

review.reviewBody: Ohkay, so I don't have cheesecloth but I do have a 4 cup coffeemaker so I cut the recipe down to work that way (brewed like Starbucks, two tablespoons per cup--I used Caffe Verona blend) and I added the cinnamon stick and clove to my grounds in the.....cone filter. After it brewed, I stirred in the (Splenda) brown sugar, vanilla and my own homemade chocolate syrup. Honestly? This was heaven. I didn't have whipped cream for the top but next time I make this, I'll be sure to have it on hand. This was wonderful and quite a treat. I did add just a touch of warmed half-n-half because I can't drink my coffee black.

I needed a pick-me-up for this chilly May afternoon (46 degrees!). This hit the spot. I loved the clove and cinnamon. I cut back just a bit on the brown sugar. I sprinkled a little allspice on the whipped cream. I don't have cheesecloth, so I put the cinnamon and clove in the carafe of my coffee maker and let it sit for about 5 minutes after it brewed. Then I stirred in the brown sugar, vanilla and chocolate. I'll definitely make this again.

I don't have a cheese cloth so I threw the cinnamon stick and the clove along with the coffee into my Ninja Coffee Bar cone and brewed it that way. I topped it off with fat free whip cream and a bit of chocolate syrup, I enjoyed it.

OhmyGod!!! what a wonderful recipe. The 2nd time I customized it to our taste buds for a more robust taste: increased sugar to 1/2 cup, increased cloves to 2, increased coffee beans to 3/4 cup... to die for. The 3rd time I ran out of whipped cream to I whipped 8 oz of heavy cream and mixed it with 4 teaspoons of sifted confectioner's sugar. Thank you for a wonderful recipe!!!

I thought this was good. I am going to add it to my recipe box with the winter recipes because adding the clove reminded me of lightly spiced Christmas coffees. Or, I might try it again leaving out the clove. The only thing I changed was using an equal amount of instant coffee and I used lite chocolate syrup. I just poured it through a strainer then instead of using the cheese cloth method. The spiced coffee gave a nice warmth this chilly morning.

I was looking for something different for an all-night study session from the ingredients in my kitchen. I made this recipe without chocolate and with steamed milk in a french press. It worked wonderfully! The flavor is very nice.

I made this for my husband and myself. I followed the recipe for the most part. I used about 1/2 cup of vanilla syrup instead of extract and I poured it straight through my cone filtered coffee maker when it was ready. Topped with cool whip this was delicious.

Really good on a cold Michigan morning. I just made this in my coffeemaker by putting all the spices and coffee together and brewing the coffee. The chocolate syrup was a nice touch. Making this in the coffeemaker made the process easier and the end result was super-tasty. Thanks for sharing!

A nice version of Mexican - style coffee drink. I used unsweetened cacao mixed with some hot water instead of chocolate syrup. I was also too lazy to whip my cream. I liked it and so did my daughter. Thank you for the recipe.

This is so tasty! I made it as a pick me up for two friends that were having a rough day. They really enjoyed it! I omitted the clove as I was out and this was a last minute thing. I used homemade chocolate syrup. I also used some cinnamon flavored coffee and a vanilla coffee k-cups.

I like this drink. The spices were subtle to me, certainly not overpowering, and the chocolate was the perfect amount. I can see this being addictive in the wintertime, maybe because cloves and cinnamon make me think of the winter holidays. My biggest problem was the straining. I didn't have cheesecloth, so I used coffee filters which took time. I may try brewing this in my coffee pot next time to see if the taste is similar. It would certainly be easier.
Making plans to make again.
Followed exactly as written. Delicious!
Delicious! Thank you for sharing this recipe! :)
This reciepe for coffe is great
This was delicious! I followed the recipe as written using Starbucks Espresso grind. It was great for a cold winter afternoon.
Oh my oh my. This is so good. Made exactly as recipe. Usually love my coffee black, no cream or sugar. But this is a great dessert drink.

Did exactly as directions said, but didn't taste that great. By the time it was strained the coffee was cooled down a lot. Had strong taste from either the clove or cinnamon, couldn't tell for sure which. Won't be making again.
Made this morning for cinco de mayo. Wow too good.

This is an awesome recipe, I normally strain my coffee with a cheesecloth colador anyways. It was very good, the only problem is that right now I only have two coffee drinkers in the house so I now have to make it when I have people over, otherwise, I just drink way to much coffee in one day, lol
